prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 96-120 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a rotting undead minotaur, grey-green decaying hide torn open to show white ribs on one side, a bull skull head with two short horns curving out to the sides, one whole and one snapped off halfway, the same two horns in every cell, glowing pale green eye sockets, a tattered loincloth, holding one big rusted cleaver; in the idle cell the cleaver hangs low in one hand; the horn tips well below the top of the grey box, centred in its own cell, the whole cleaver well inside its cell in every cell. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: its bull skull with glowing green eye sockets and the broken horn is readable.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, stepping forward toward the heroes at the end of a downward chop: the cleaver in both hands, its blade low in front of him at knee height, the body leaning in, the whole cleaver well inside the middle cell (not raised overhead, not reaching the cell edge), facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the skull head thrown back, the cleaver held up across the chest in both hands, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Use a strong diagonal line of action through the whole body, shift the weight clearly onto one leg, twist the torso and swing the cleaver with the elbows bent, so every reaching part stays well inside its own cell. Draw only the parts and clothing named in the description, the same in every cell: no cape, cloak, scarf or extra cloth, and no slash trail, smear or motion lines. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, standing on two feet, both feet on the ground line. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, a nose ring, a harness, brown fur, a double-bladed axe, a cape, two whole horns, long horns, a hornless skull.
